trust_decision.summary: Path-based authorization (HTTP permission policies, Keycloak PEP, servlet web.xml constraints, OIDC tenant-by-path, CSRF token path) is decided on Vert.x normalizedPath() with only literal ';' matrix params stripped, while downstream handlers fully decode (%2F, %5C, %3B, %00, %25xx), so the security layer and the resource handler can see different paths.

landing_point.why: The summary is about auth/authz bypass via path normalization; quarkus.http.auth.permission path matching is the central HTTP authorization check and is where normalizedPath() is matched against configured paths.

fix_sites.entry_point: public helper HttpSecurityUtils (new normalizePath added next to pathWithoutMatrixParams, fix.diff:645-699); used by all sites below
any HTTP request matched against quarkus.http.auth.permission.*.paths (main router, management interface, applies-to=JAXRS) and path-based auth-mechanism selection
build of the permission path matcher from quarkus.http.auth.permission.*.paths config
HTTP request with quarkus-keycloak-authorization policy enforcer enabled (PathConfig lookup)
same Keycloak PEP request; path handed to Keycloak's PolicyEnforcer via HttpRequest.getRelativePath()
HTTP request with OIDC multitenancy, tenant id taken from a path segment (DefaultStaticTenantResolver)
REST request with quarkus-rest-csrf and quarkus.rest-csrf.create-token-path set
HTTP request to a servlet with web.xml / annotation security constraints
fix_sites.module_kind: separate extension, second authorization implementation (servlet constraints)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Servlet constraints, Keycloak PEP, OIDC tenant selection and CSRF token path are separate extensions with their own matching semantics (and tenant/CSRF selection is not itself an authorization check), so a solver can argue the report is about quarkus.http.auth.permission only.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Literal ';' matrix params must still be stripped and permission paths must still match; Vert.x-normalized unreserved-char encodings (/api/adm%69n) must still be authorized normally (200 for admin), dot segments must still resolve, and the router's own path must still be matched so that decode-then-removeDots does not move a /admin/..;/public request into a permit prefix (upstream later added this guard).
